release.title: Gross domestic product: June 2026 quarter
release.headline: Gross domestic product rose 0.2 percent in the June 2026 quarter compared with the March 2026 quarter.

executive_summary.text: Real GDP (production measure, seasonally adjusted) rose 0.2% in the June 2026 quarter, after 0.9% in the March 2026 quarter.
In the year ended June 2026, real GDP was 1.7% higher than in the year ended June 2025 (annual average growth, from actual values).
Seasonally adjusted real GDP in the June 2026 quarter was 2.6% higher than in the June 2025 quarter. This compares one quarter with the same quarter a year earlier; it is not annual average growth.

headline_metrics.label: Quarterly GDP growth (production, real, seasonally adjusted)
Annual change in quarterly GDP (production, real, seasonally adjusted)

context.text: The expenditure measure of real GDP (seasonally adjusted) rose 0.4% in the quarter. The production and expenditure measures are estimated independently and usually differ.
Real GDP per person (production, seasonally adjusted) was $13,410 in the June 2026 quarter, against $13,399 in the March 2026 quarter (+0.1%, calculated here from the two published values).
Nominal GDP (expenditure measure, current prices, seasonally adjusted) was $115.8 billion in the quarter. Nominal values include price changes.

previous_comparison.note: GDP growth is compared with earlier publications in the revisions table.

revisions.note: 7 of 159 quarters of published quarterly growth shared with Gross domestic product: March 2026 quarter were revised. National accounts are revised as more complete information arrives.

corrections.note: No earlier distinct statistical capture is stored for this publication.

definitions: Gross domestic product (GDP) measures the value of goods and services produced in New Zealand. Stats NZ's headline is the production measure in chain-volume terms (real), seasonally adjusted.

Three growth measures are shown and are never interchangeable: quarterly growth compares a quarter with the previous quarter (seasonally adjusted); the annual change of a quarter compares it with the same quarter a year earlier (seasonally adjusted); annual average growth compares the four quarters to date with the four before them (actual values). Stats NZ's release page calls the last one 'Annual growth'.

Chain-volume (real) values remove the effect of price changes; current-price (nominal) values do not. Seasonally adjusted and actual values are different series. They are kept on separate charts. The chain-volume reference year is not stated in the captured CSV metadata and is not assigned here.
notes: The production and expenditure measures are estimated independently from different data and usually differ; neither is a correction of the other.
National accounts are revised as more complete information arrives, and seasonal adjustment re-estimates history every quarter. The first-published and latest figures for a quarter can differ.
Per-person values divide GDP by Stats NZ's population estimate. Stats NZ's file declares an inconsistent magnitude for some per-capita series; values are shown in dollars as published.
This page describes published statistics only. It makes no forecast and no statement about policy.

series.name: Quarterly GDP growth (production, real, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: Percentage change in seasonally adjusted real production GDP from the previous quarter, as published by Stats NZ (1 d.p.).

series.name: Annual change in quarterly GDP (production, real, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: Percentage change in seasonally adjusted real production GDP from the same quarter a year earlier, as published by Stats NZ (1 d.p.). Not annual average growth.

series.name: Annual average GDP growth (production, real)
series.definition: Percentage change in real production GDP for the year ended in the quarter against the previous year ended in the same quarter (sum of four actual quarters), as published by Stats NZ (1 d.p.). The release page's 'Annual growth' chart.

series.name: Quarterly GDP growth (expenditure, real, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: Percentage change in seasonally adjusted real expenditure GDP from the previous quarter, as published by Stats NZ (1 d.p.).
